title: Factorise a monic quadratic with mixed signs

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

student_prompt: Show your working and give your answer in factorised form.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: The numbers 4 and 3 are right, but the larger number must be positive so the sum is +1.
Your brackets give the constant term but lose the middle x term. Check the two inside/outside products.

hint_ladder.title: What does a negative constant imply?
hint_ladder.prompt: A negative constant in a monic quadratic means the bracket constants have opposite signs. Think about which sign should go with the larger magnitude.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Find factor pairs for the absolute value of the constant, then choose signs so the middle term has the correct direction.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Many students get the two magnitudes right but reverse the signs. Check whether your bracket pair creates the stated middle term.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For x^2 + bx - c, use opposite signs. The larger magnitude controls the sign of the middle term. Apply this pattern to your expression; do not copy an example.

expected_solution_steps.expression: 4 and -3 multiply to -12 and add to 1
common_errors: chooses 6 and -2 because the product is correct
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is choosing which factor should be positive and which should be negative.

common_errors: does not check the middle term
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is checking that the middle term is +x, not -x.

mark_scheme_notes: Award 1 mark for identifying 4 and -3; 1 mark for the correct factorised expression.
examiner_report_notes: Common errors expected: reversed signs, product-only checking, missing verification of the middle term.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, how will you decide which factor is positive?
